findings.description: The catch block returns e.message directly to the UI. Raw internal error messages (which may include stack details, internal paths, or implementation specifics from the Harness/runCodingVertical layer) could leak sensitive information to callers. Consider mapping known error types to safe, generic messages and logging the original error server-side.

The non-success branch exposes result.outcome.loop_result.termination_reason in the user-facing error string. Depending on what termination_reason contains (e.g., internal agent loop diagnostics, model/provider identifiers, or sanitized tool output), this could leak internal state. Verify that termination_reason is safe to surface to UI consumers.

summary: The controller is a thin wrapper around runCodingVertical with no injection, path traversal, SSRF, prototype pollution, or ReDoS exposure. Control flow and result shaping are correct. The only concerns are minor information-leakage risks from forwarding raw exception messages and internal termination_reason values to the UI; these are low severity and do not block the requirement.
